text: <!channel> :rotating_light: Seeing elevated response times on checkout-db-primary. P95 latency jumped from 150ms to 3.5s. Starting incident investigation.

attachments.title: checkout-db-primary High CPU
attachments.text:
Severity: SEV-2
Service: checkout-db-primary
Assigned to: James Rodriguez

text: Taking IC role. <@U001>, continue investigation. <@U003> can you check if we're seeing customer impact?
Checking support queue now. We have 12 new tickets in the last 5 minutes about slow checkout. Usually see 2-3 per hour.
Database CPU is at 94%. Looking at slow query log now...
*Status Update*: Declared SEV-2 incident. Database performance degraded, customer checkout affected. War room: <https://meet.company.com/incident-847>
Found it! There's a query hitting the orders table without using the index. Scanning 2M+ rows on every execution.
Oh no... that's from the merchant dashboard feature we deployed 2 hours ago. The index should be on (merchant_id, status, created_at) but I only created (merchant_id, created_at).
Options: 1. Kill the queries manually (temporary) 2. Rate limit the merchant dashboard endpoint 3. Rollback the deployment 4. Add the missing index (takes ~5 mins)
I vote rollback while we add the index properly in a fix. Fastest path to recovery.
Agreed. <@U004> start rollback. <@U001> can you add rate limiting as backup in case rollback doesn't fully resolve?
:tada: Query count dropped immediately. CPU back to 23%. P95 latency at 180ms.
*Status Update*: Rollback complete. Metrics returning to normal. Will monitor for 30 minutes before declaring all-clear.
PR ready for review: <https://github.com/company/checkout-service/pull/1842|PR #1842> Added proper index + query explain test. Running load tests now.
:white_check_mark: *INCIDENT RESOLVED* - All metrics stable. Thanks everyone for quick response!
